pdmat evaluate

Documents/pdmat/evaluate

Purpose

Section titled “Purpose”

Evaluate a pdmat object at a finite parameter point.

Syntax

Section titled “Syntax”

Arguments

Section titled “Arguments”
ArgumentDescription
AA pdmat object.
ptFinite real scalar for one parameter, such as 0.25, or a row vector with one entry per parameter, such as [0.25 12]. The point must lie inside the grid bounds.

Output

Section titled “Output”

val is a numeric matrix with size A.MatrixSize.

Description

Section titled “Description”

For coefficient-backed data on one cell, evaluate applies local Bernstein interpolation. For degree-one scalar data on [rho0,rho1],

A(ρ)=(1−α)A0+αA1,α=ρ−ρ1(c)ρ1(c+1)−ρ1(c).A(\rho)=(1-\alpha)A_0+\alpha A_1,\qquad \alpha=\frac{\rho-\rho_1^{(c)}}{\rho_1^{(c+1)}-\rho_1^{(c)}}.A(ρ)=(1−α)A0​+αA1​,α=ρ1(c+1)​−ρ1(c)​ρ−ρ1(c)​​.

For matrix-valued data, the same formula is applied entrywise to each stored coefficient matrix. Function-backed objects keep the exact MATLAB function handle and call it directly.

Examples

Section titled “Examples”

Function-call form

Section titled “Function-call form”

At rho = 0.25, the public forward coordinate is alpha = 0.25, so the value is 0.75*2 + 0.25*4.

Dot-call form

Section titled “Dot-call form”

The dot-call form is equivalent to evaluate(A, pt) and is often convenient in interactive MATLAB sessions.

Function-backed evaluation

Section titled “Function-backed evaluation”

Function-backed objects route evaluation through the retained function handle.

Validation And Errors

Section titled “Validation And Errors”
  • Bad point shape or nonfinite values raise pdmat:InvalidPoint.
  • Points outside grid bounds raise pdmat:PointOutOfBounds.
  • Function-handle failures during evaluation raise pdmat:InvalidFunctionValue.
